info.name: Plantsec M1 — Florensic backend
info.description:
Milestone M1 of the Florensic backend: auth, /me, species catalogue, plants, care actions, today's tasks.

Run the folders top to bottom. Requests save what later requests need (tokens, species_id, plant_id, task_id) into collection variables automatically.

The only manual step: after '1.1 Sign up', copy the 6-digit OTP from the API logs into the `otp_code` variable (see docs/testing-in-postman.md).

Errors always look like {"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}.

item.name: 3.4 Species by id
item.description: Full card: common_name(s), latin_name, summary, difficulty, light, water, temperature, humidity, tags, traits, common_issues, care_tips, default_care. Unknown id → 404 species_not_found.

request.description:
Public. For the moment someone decides an identification is wrong and starts typing the name they meant. Returns {items, query}.

Our own catalogue is matched first (scientific name, common names and recorded synonyms, case-insensitive), ranked prefix > word start > substring; those rows carry source="catalogue" and a species_id you can pass straight to 3.4 or 4.1. iNaturalist fills the rest of the list with plants we don't carry yet: source="inaturalist", species_id null, external_id set — hand either kind to 8b.2 to get a species_id.

Every row is a species. A genus ("Monstera") is never suggested: nobody owns a genus, and a care card written for thirty plants at once helps no one.

matched_term is the name the query actually matched, so "tulsi" comes back with matched_term "Tulsi" — show it, or the suggestion looks like a non sequitur.

Two things to know. Queries shorter than three characters are answered from the catalogue alone (iNaturalist allows ~60 requests a minute for our whole server). And the endpoint learns: when iNaturalist names a plant we already carry, the row comes back as ours, with its species_id, and the word you typed is remembered as one of that species' common names — so the next person who types it matches our catalogue directly.

201 with the full Plant. Defaults: watering every 7 days (or the species baseline), 220 ml, check-in every 14 days, reminders on at 08:00. Since the health-score cutover there is no starting score: `health_score` and `health_band` are null until something scores the plant, which for a plant kept with `photo_id` is the identification itself and otherwise the first check-in. Unknown species → 404 species_not_found.

item.name: 8.4 Resume plant (409 on an active plant)

request.description: Resuming a paused plant returns 200 with care_status active, the score it already had (since the cutover a resume no longer throws it back to 70 — the returning check-in is believed outright instead), and a fresh care-plan revision with trigger 'resumed'. The plant you have been testing with is active, so this request is expected to return 409 plant_not_paused. No endpoint pauses a plant: PATCH /v1/plants/{id} does not accept care_status, and a plant is paused only by the 03:00 UTC care.missed_check_ins sweep when a check-in window closes with no update. To see the 200, either let that sweep run, or pause the plant by hand: docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U plantsec -d plantsec -c "update plants set care_status='paused' where id='<plant_id>'" (credentials from docker-compose.yml). A paused plant keeps its number and loses its band: `health_score` stands and `health_band` is null.

exec: pm.test('409 plant_not_paused on an already-active plant', function () {

item.name: 8b Correct a plant's species
item.description:
The owner says the identification is wrong. Search a name (8b.1), turn the row they picked into a species_id (8b.2), correct the plant (8b.3), and watch the care plan follow (8b.4).

8b.2 is the only slow step, and only the first time anyone resolves a given plant: drafting a species we don't carry is one text-model call, about ten seconds, and answers 201. Every later resolve of that plant — by anyone, under any of its names — is a lookup that answers 200.

request.description: Same call as 3.5, kept here so this folder runs on its own. The test script saves the first row whole — source, external_id, scientific_name, matched_term and species_id — because 8b.2 sends a suggestion back exactly as it was received.

exec: pm.test('200 with at least one suggestion', function () {

request.description:
Auth. Sends the suggestion 8b.1 saved, back as it came:

{"source": "inaturalist", "species_id": null, "external_id": "181060",
 "scientific_name": "Ocimum tenuiflorum", "matched_term": "Tulsi"}

The pre-request script assembles that from the saved variables, because a catalogue row carries a species_id and no external_id and an iNaturalist row the other way round, and those have to go over as null rather than "".

Auth. 200 when we already have the plant, 201 when this call drafted it — allow about ten seconds for a 201, which is one text-model call writing the care card. Answers {species_id, scientific_name, created}.

A drafted species arrives knowing every name iNaturalist has for it, in every language, plus the word you typed. Run 8b.1 and 8b.2 again with a different name for the same plant and you get the same species_id back with created=false: it is never drafted twice.

503 species_draft_unavailable means the model, GBIF or the day's budget said no; retry later. 429 species_draft_quota_exceeded means this account has drafted its five new species for the day — plants we already carry still resolve. A catalogue row whose species we no longer have is 404 species_not_found, and a scientific_name that is not a name at all is 422.

request.description:
Auth, owner only. 200 with the full Plant under its new species, so you can replace local state from the response.

It also writes a species_corrected care event ("old name → new name", visible in 4.6), relabels this plant's training rows with what the owner said, and asks for a fresh care plan. Sending the species the plant already has is a no-op: same 200, no event, no revision — so confirming an identification and correcting it are the same call.

item.name: 8c Home feed
item.description: The home screen in one request: local climate, next-plant suggestions, what changed lately, and what is blooming nearby (home-feed-design). Works on any account — a fresh one still answers 200 — but `climate` and `blooming_nearby` stay null/[] until it has a home cell, which a located photo upload sets (folder 6). `changes` fills in once a check-in (folder 8) has landed.

request.description:
Auth. 200 with the four cards: `climate` (one line of copy plus the 30-day numbers, or null without a home cell), `suggestions` (catalogue species scored against what you already keep), `changes` (what your plants did in check-ins over the last 90 days — including `flowering`, from checkin.v2 — empty until folder 8 has run), and `blooming_nearby` (species iNaturalist saw in flower near your home cell this month, or [] without one). `meta.attribution` always carries both licence lines, Open-Meteo and iNaturalist, even when their cards are empty.

The whole document is cached per user for an hour: opening the app again costs nothing until then. A finished check-in (8.2/8.3) invalidates the cache on its way out, so a GET here right after one sees the new change immediately rather than waiting out the hour.

item.name: 9 Cleanup (run last — destructive)
item.description: Soft-deletes. Run these only when you are finished: afterwards the plant and then the whole account return 404/401 everywhere. To start over, run 1.1 Sign up with a new email.

item.name: 9.2 DELETE /me (soft delete)
item.description: Soft-deletes the account and revokes refresh tokens. Afterwards every authenticated call returns 401 and signing up with the same email returns 409 account_deleted. Run this only at the very end.
